receiver.message_back:
Dear Counsel,

Thank you for sending the Seller’s initial draft. Buyer has reviewed and has several comments.

Most importantly, based on Buyer’s preliminary assessment of the Company and the limited protections currently reflected in the draft, Buyer is not prepared to proceed at USD 45,000,000. Buyer proposes a purchase price of USD 36,000,000, payable at Closing and subject to customary adjustments for cash, debt, working capital, transaction expenses, and similar items.

The current draft is also too limited for a share purchase. Please revise to include customary buyer protections, including unqualified financial statement representations, full title/capitalization and authority representations, representations regarding undisclosed liabilities, taxes, compliance with law, material contracts, litigation, employees, IP, and absence of material adverse change. Buyer will also require customary closing conditions, including satisfactory confirmatory diligence, accuracy of representations, covenant compliance, required consents, no material adverse effect, and delivery of customary closing certificates.

We also propose that Closing occur only after completion of Buyer’s confirmatory diligence and satisfaction or waiver of all conditions, with an outside date 60 days after signing. Finally, please add customary indemnification provisions for breaches of representations, warranties, covenants, pre-closing taxes, and excluded liabilities, with baskets, caps, survival periods, and fraud carve-outs to be discussed.

The confidentiality provision is acceptable in concept, subject to customary exceptions for disclosures to Buyer’s affiliates, representatives, financing sources, regulators, and as otherwise required by law.

Please circulate a revised draft reflecting the above.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP

drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Dear Counsel,

Thank you for your comments. We have enclosed a revised draft reflecting Seller's good-faith movement on economics and a more developed SPA framework.

On price, Seller is not prepared to transact at USD 36,000,000 based on the Company's performance and the competitive process to date. In the interest of moving this forward, Seller has revised the purchase price to USD 40,500,000, payable at Closing and subject to customary adjustments. Seller is prepared to discuss the specific working capital methodology promptly so the parties can avoid open-ended post-closing disputes.

We have also added customary representations, closing conditions, confidentiality exceptions, and indemnity provisions. As reflected in the draft, Seller's position is that confirmatory diligence should be run on an expedited basis, closing should not be subject to a broad subjective diligence condition, and indemnity should be subject to customary materiality, survival, basket, and cap limitations. We included a 45-day outside date, which should be sufficient given Buyer's existing review and the targeted nature of remaining diligence.

Please let us know if Buyer can engage on this basis. We are available to discuss the principal business points this week.

Best regards,
Aldous Finch LLP

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 40,500,000 for the Shares, payable in immediately available funds at Closing, subject to customary adjustments for cash, indebtedness, normalized working capital and unpaid transaction expenses as finally determined in accordance with a mutually agreed closing statement process. The parties shall cooperate in good faith prior to signing to agree the target working capital amount and related accounting principles, which shall be consistent with the Company's historical practices.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur as promptly as practicable, and in any event within five Business Days, following satisfaction or waiver of the conditions set forth in this Agreement. Buyer shall complete its confirmatory diligence on an expedited basis, and in no event later than 20 days after signing. The outside date shall be 45 days after signing, subject to extension only to the extent necessary to obtain any required governmental approval that is being pursued diligently by the parties.

3. Representations of Seller. Seller represents and warrants to Buyer, subject to the limitations, qualifications and disclosure schedules to be agreed by the parties, that: (a) Seller has good and valid title to the Shares, free and clear of liens other than transfer restrictions under applicable securities laws and liens arising through Buyer; (b) Seller has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement, and this Agreement constitutes a valid and binding obligation of Seller; (c) the Shares constitute all of the issued and outstanding equity interests of the Company and have been duly authorized and validly issued; (d) the Company's financial statements fairly present, in all material respects, the financial condition and results of operations of the Company as of the dates and for the periods indicated therein, in accordance with the accounting principles historically applied by the Company, consistently applied; (e) except as reflected in the financial statements or disclosed to Buyer, the Company has no material liabilities required to be reflected on a balance sheet prepared in accordance with such accounting principles; (f) the Company is, and during the applicable limitation period has been, in material compliance with applicable laws; (g) the Company has timely filed material tax returns required to be filed and has paid all material taxes due and payable, subject to customary exceptions for taxes being contested in good faith; (h) the material contracts disclosed to Buyer are valid and in force in all material respects, and neither the Company nor, to Seller's knowledge, any counterparty is in material breach thereof; (i) there is no material litigation pending or, to Seller's knowledge, threatened against the Company; (j) the Company is in material compliance with applicable employment laws and has no pending material labor dispute; (k) to Seller's knowledge, the Company owns or has the right to use the intellectual property material to the conduct of its business as currently conducted; and (l) since the date of the most recent financial statements, there has not occurred any Material Adverse Effect. For purposes of this Agreement, 'Material Adverse Effect' shall exclude effects resulting from general economic, industry, market, legal or political conditions, changes in law or accounting standards, acts of war, terrorism, pandemics or natural disasters, or the announcement or pendency of the transactions contemplated hereby, except to the extent disproportionately affecting the Company relative to similarly situated businesses.

4. Confidentiality. The terms of this Agreement and all negotiations relating hereto are confidential and shall not be disclosed by either party except (a) as required by law, regulation, legal process or the rules of any governmental authority or securities exchange, (b) with the prior written consent of the other party, or (c) to such party's affiliates, directors, officers, employees, representatives, advisors, financing sources and prospective financing sources who have a need to know such information in connection with the transactions contemplated hereby and are informed of the confidential nature of such information; provided that the disclosing party shall be responsible for any breach of this Section by such recipients.

5. Conditions to Closing. Buyer's obligation to close shall be subject to: (a) the fundamental representations being true and correct in all material respects and the other representations being true and correct except where the failure to be true and correct would not reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect; (b) Seller having performed in all material respects its covenants required to be performed prior to Closing; (c) receipt of required governmental approvals and material third-party consents identified on the disclosure schedules; (d) no law or order prohibiting Closing; (e) no Material Adverse Effect having occurred after signing; (f) delivery of customary officer and secretary certificates; and (g) payoff at Closing of Company indebtedness identified for payoff, if any, from the purchase price proceeds. Buyer's confirmatory diligence shall not constitute a separate closing condition except for specific matters identified in writing by Buyer during the diligence period that reveal a material breach of the representations or a Material Adverse Effect.

6. Indemnification. From and after Closing, Seller shall indemnify Buyer for losses finally incurred by Buyer arising out of breaches of Seller's representations and warranties, breaches of Seller's covenants, pre-Closing taxes of the Company, and any excluded liabilities expressly identified in this Agreement. General representations shall survive for 12 months following Closing; fundamental representations and tax matters shall survive for the applicable statute of limitations plus 60 days; and covenants shall survive in accordance with their terms. Seller shall have no liability for breaches of general representations unless aggregate covered losses exceed a deductible basket equal to 1.0% of the purchase price, after which only amounts in excess of the basket shall be recoverable. Seller's aggregate liability for breaches of general representations shall not exceed 10% of the purchase price. Fundamental representations, taxes, covenant breaches and fraud shall not be subject to the general representation cap, except that Seller's aggregate liability shall not exceed the purchase price other than in the case of actual fraud. Indemnifiable losses shall exclude punitive, special, exemplary and consequential damages except to the extent awarded to a third party.
